This article and associated research paper ought be required reading on this topic: Data Mining Reveals How The “Down-Vote” Leads To A Vicious Circle Of Negative Feedback

Essentially downvoting seems to do little more than damage online communities. The data show it really doesn't work as a punitive measure and is actually correlated with those who get downvoted not only sticking around, but posting progressively lower quality stuff. And on top of that they also become more likely to downvote other users in turn which creates a nasty domino effect.

An issue that was not mentioned is that it also seems, in the long run, to result in hiveminds in communities. Some people are always going to use downvotes as a petty dislike or "take this!" button. Trying to educate people not to is akin to trying to teach people to control their emotions. In other words it's going to fail. But when people do use it as a dislike button it ends up censoring out submissions and comments which run against the grain of a community. As a result of this the only things that end up getting actively discussed in a community in the longrun are things everybody already agrees to. Great for insecure folks seeking affirmation that their beliefs are 'correct', not so great for any sort of reasonably intelligent and interesting conversation.

My suggestion:

Make downvoats limited - people tend to spend what they never run out of quite freely.

I think the least painful way to implement this might be:

  1. make a job that accrues downvoats for users (IE, 1 gained each 3 hours, max 5 downvoats - you'll likely need to alter an existing table to store it, adding downvoat tally and last updated timestamp. numbers are arbitrary in example - you'd probably want them variable based on account age or w/e. like: newish accounts accrue 1 downvoat per 48hours, max 2 or something.

  2. run the job individually on user log in.
    ( this avoids setting up cron to batch run jobs, potentially on dead accounts, and spreads the load out. )

  3. re run the job periodically based on a client side pull
    ( perhaps per downvoat cast, or per 4 hours of whatever. - this keeps active and long term logged in accounts up to date)

  4. existing downvoat logic would need to be altered to check and decrement a user's downvoat tally.
    ( likely the most annoying bit of this scheme. )

  5. optionally - IP ban anyone hammering the job for X hours
    (the downvoat job should exit immediately if it was recently run anyway.. ...but people will be idiots. If it is an exposed interface, someone will eventually use it to attack if you don't throttle. )

Also: whatever interval is set to generate a downvoat, I would 'reset' the clock on when a user at max has 'spent' a downvoat, possibly + a couple hours - This will encourage people to spend them when merited, rather than as they accrue.

What is the purpose of voting?

From my standpoint, the purpose of voting is so that the content that the most users enjoy is featured, while content the majority of users don't enjoy is played down. Voat has never defined any other purpose for upvotes or downvotes, despite some people are still using Reddit's definition. But if what we want is the best content to float and the worst content to sink, the most meaningful use of a downvote is 'I did not enjoy this post'. For whatever reason - 'the cat isn't cute', 'the joke isn't funny', 'the news is from a biased source', or 'I prefer to live in an echo chamber'.

There seems to be a push to say 'dissenting opinions deserve to be featured, as well', and I agree. But the thing is, if the majority of us feel that way, there's nothing wrong with using upvote as "like" and downvote as "dislike". If I upvote things I disagree with as long as they're meaningful contribution, and everyone else does, as well, unpopular opinions get their moment in the spotlight.

But maybe not everyone feels the way I do. Maybe some people don't ever want to see a dissenting opinion. If those people turn out to be the majority, why would we force the site to work in a way that runs counter to what the majority of users want? That sounds a whole lot like what Reddit does.

We're obviously a big enough group now, though, that we won't come to consensus here.

So I'm approaching this from a standpoint that the only issue that needs to be addressed is vote manipulation. A world where up and down are just 'I want to see more like this' and 'I want to see less like this', and that's the way it should be, and if you post things people don't enjoy reading, those things don't get featured. My solution doesn't get into head-y 'people aren't using downvotes the way I think they should and I'm unhappy you're not forcing them to' - we're just trying to make sure the score a post receives is actually reflective of the way the community it's posted to views it.

When you think of it that way, to me, it becomes simple. Make votes a subverse-based currency. If my comments or posts in /v/funny net upvotes, I get a number of upvotes and downvotes to spend, but only in that sub. We can change the ratios - we may want to give people 10 upvotes to pass out for every upvote they get, and only 1 downvote (or 0.5 downvote, or 0.01 downvote, or whatever - or maybe make it customizable by sub), but ultimately, this makes subs devoted to getting upvotes worthless (as the 'currency' you gain there doesn't transfer to other subs), and it totally defeats brigading, as even if I've got a billion upvotes on /v/antiskub, I can't use them to vote on /v/proskub. It also restores the impetus to get involved and post that we lost when we removed the site-wide restrictions.

From there, let the individual communities decide what upvotes and downvotes mean for their users.

TLDR: Instead of sitewide restrictions, make them subwide. You can only vote in subs you're a valued contributor in, so you can't brigade. Subs where the majority want an echo chamber can have it, but those users have limited power in subs that want varied discussion.

Suggestion: Everybody, regardless of amount of participation in the site (or earned CCP), gets a minimum number of downvoats per hour/day/month or whatever. This would encourage users to use them sparingly to help fight SPAM and other forms of abuse.

If you ask me how i'd change it, i do have some ideas but i need to warn beforehand that it'd be an entirely different concept.

So, with that out of the way, the first thing i'd need t say is that there is a disconnect between votes regarding submissions and comments. As a rule, voting on submissions serves to give more or less visibility to it. The reasons for you to do it one way or the other regarding a specific submission are various. You can like it or dislike it, agree or disagree, think it's interesting or funny or cool or whatever.

Now, to me that sounds fine but the issue is when the same system is used for comments. People don't find it acceptable when others use the downvoat as a disagree button and i think that's the crux of the problem.

So, my personal opinion is that an ideal voting system would take in account what your comment was meant to convey and what the person voting on it meant with his vote. What this means is that i envision voting not on a simple up or down fashion but on a handful of possible choices. Such as like vs dislike, agree vs disagree, true vs false, funny vs not funny, interesting vs uninteresting, etc. You'd only get to pick one and there would be different effects your choice would have on the comment's ranking.

Voat itself could rank the importance of these categories, so that a downvoat on the agreement scale would matter less than a downvoat on the fact scale. But to make it even more interesting, subverses themselves could be able to display their own list of comment ranks which would combine with voat's own rank to change how voting would impact a comment on different subverses. Not just that, i'd say that subverses themselves could have a couple of ranks free of choice, independent from voat's ranks. These ranks could serve to convey what each subverse were looking for in comments. So, if in most mainstream subverses the ranks would go for standard voat choices (for instance, v/science would rank facts highest or TIL would rank interesting highest), niche subverses could incorporate in their rank categories that pertained to their content.

Finally, the commenter himself, when making the comment would be able to choose the category they wished their comment to be judged primarily for. So, you'd mark either as opinion, fact, humor or whatever else, from voat's own categories or the subverse's own. This could or not be shown to others but the result would be that choosing the intent of your comment would add to the effect other people's voting choice would have on it.

In the end, this would mean that each vote could be valued different depending on the subverse's most valued comment types, the commenter's intent and the voater's judgment. Lining up or not with each set of rank modifiers would make each vote add more or less to its ranking. I'd still show the total of votes up or down but would completely do away with a numbered ranking since each vote would have a different value, instead going for an arrow that fill up or down and grow or diminish.

Oh, and i'd do this just for comments, submissions should stay the same.
